audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 15, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Maximum audit for Amalek memory, herem vocabulary, command to kill infants and animals, Kenite separation, Saul's selective destruction and spoil, Divine regret, sacrifice/obedience rhetoric, fear of people, robe sign, theological change-of-mind tension, Agag speech, Samuel's dismemberment, and genocide-misuse safeguards.

verses.restored: Samuel said to Saul, YHWH sent me to anoint you as king over his people Israel. Now listen to voice of words of YHWH.

familiar.text: Samuel also said unto Saul, The LORD sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the LORD.

modern.text: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל אֹתִ֨י שָׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ לִמְשָׁחֳךָ֣ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ עַל עַמּ֖וֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֣ה שְׁמַ֔ע לְק֖וֹל דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Thus says YHWH of armies: I have attended to what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on way when he came up from Egypt.

familiar.text: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.

modern.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they ambushed them on their way up from Egypt.

original.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת פָּקַ֕דְתִּי אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה עֲמָלֵ֖ק לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר שָׂ֥ם לוֹ֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בַּעֲלֹת֖וֹ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that belongs to him. Do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.

familiar.text: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.

modern.text: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”

original.text: עַתָּה֩ לֵ֨ךְ וְהִכִּֽיתָ֜ה אֶת עֲמָלֵ֗ק וְהַֽחֲרַמְתֶּם֙ אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר ל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ל עָלָ֑יו וְהֵמַתָּ֞ה מֵאִ֣ישׁ עַד אִשָּׁ֗ה מֵֽעֹלֵל֙ וְעַד יוֹנֵ֔ק מִשּׁ֣וֹר וְעַד שֶׂ֔ה מִגָּמָ֖ל וְעַד חֲמֽוֹר

verses.restored: Saul summoned people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.

familiar.text: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.

modern.text: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.

original.text: וַיְשַׁמַּ֤ע שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּפְקְדֵם֙ בַּטְּלָאִ֔ים מָאתַ֥יִם אֶ֖לֶף רַגְלִ֑י וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים אֶת אִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Saul came to city of Amalek and lay in wait in wadi.

familiar.text: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.

modern.text: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל עַד עִ֣יר עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיָּ֖רֶב בַּנָּֽחַל

verses.restored: Saul said to Kenites, Go, turn aside, come down from midst of Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed covenant-kindness to all children of Israel when they came up from Egypt. Kenites turned aside from midst of Amalek.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.

modern.text: And he warned the Kenites, “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away with them.” So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֣וּל אֶֽל הַקֵּינִ֡י לְכוּ֩ סֻּ֨רוּ רְד֜וּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ עֲמָלֵקִ֗י פֶּן אֹֽסִפְךָ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֞ה עָשִׂ֤יתָה חֶ֨סֶד֙ עִם כָּל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּעֲלוֹתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֥סַר קֵינִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ עֲמָלֵֽק

verses.restored: Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is before Egypt.

familiar.text: And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, that is over against Egypt.

modern.text: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.

original.text: וַיַּ֥ךְ שָׁא֖וּל אֶת עֲמָלֵ֑ק מֵֽחֲוִילָה֙ בּוֹאֲךָ֣ שׁ֔וּר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל פְּנֵ֥י מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: He seized Agag king of Amalek alive, and all people he devoted to destruction by edge of sword.

familiar.text: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

modern.text: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the others to destruction with the sword.

original.text: וַיִּתְפֹּ֛שׂ אֶת אֲגַ֥ג מֶֽלֶךְ עֲמָלֵ֖ק חָ֑י וְאֶת כָּל הָעָ֖ם הֶחֱרִ֥ים לְפִי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: But Saul and people spared Agag and best of sheep, cattle, second-born/fatlings, lambs, and all that was good, and they were unwilling to devote them to destruction; all despised and weak property they devoted.

familiar.text: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.

modern.text: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to destroy them, but they devoted to destruction all that was despised and worthless. Samuel Denounces Saul

original.text: וַיַּחְמֹל֩ שָׁא֨וּל וְהָעָ֜ם עַל אֲגָ֗ג וְעַל מֵיטַ֣ב הַצֹּאן֩ וְהַבָּקָ֨ר וְהַמִּשְׁנִ֤ים וְעַל הַכָּרִים֙ וְעַל כָּל הַטּ֔וֹב וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וּ הַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְכָל הַמְּלָאכָ֛ה נְמִבְזָ֥ה וְנָמֵ֖ס אֹתָ֥הּ הֶחֱרִֽימוּ

verses.restored: Word of YHWH came to Samuel, saying,

familiar.text: Then came the word of the LORD unto Samuel, saying,

modern.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not established my words. Samuel was angry/distressed, and he cried to YHWH all night.

familiar.text: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night.

modern.text: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.” And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.

original.text: נִחַ֗מְתִּי כִּֽי הִמְלַ֤כְתִּי אֶת שָׁאוּל֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי שָׁב֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְאֶת דְּבָרַ֖י לֹ֣א הֵקִ֑ים וַיִּ֨חַר֙ לִשְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּזְעַ֥ק אֶל יְהוָ֖ה כָּל הַלָּֽיְלָה

verses.restored: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in morning. It was told to Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and look, he set up for himself a monument; then he turned and crossed over and went down to Gilgal.

familiar.text: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.

modern.text: Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֧ם שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל לִקְרַ֥את שָׁא֖וּל בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִשְׁמוּאֵ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּֽא שָׁא֤וּל הַכַּרְמֶ֨לָה֙ וְהִנֵּ֨ה מַצִּ֥יב לוֹ֙ יָ֔ד וַיִּסֹּב֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔ר וַיֵּ֖רֶד הַגִּלְגָּֽל

verses.restored: Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, Blessed are you of YHWH; I have established word of YHWH.

familiar.text: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of the LORD: I have performed the commandment of the LORD.

modern.text: When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ שָׁא֗וּל בָּר֤וּךְ אַתָּה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הֲקִימֹ֖תִי אֶת דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Samuel said, Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears and sound of cattle that I hear?

familiar.text: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?

modern.text: But Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וּמֶ֛ה קֽוֹל הַצֹּ֥אן הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאָזְנָ֑י וְק֣וֹל הַבָּקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁמֵֽעַ

verses.restored: Saul said, From Amalekites they brought them, for people spared best of sheep and cattle to sacrifice to YHWH your Divine, and rest we devoted to destruction.

familiar.text: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.

modern.text: Saul answered, “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל מֵעֲמָלֵקִ֣י הֱבִיא֗וּם אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָמַ֤ל הָעָם֙ עַל מֵיטַ֤ב הַצֹּאן֙ וְהַבָּקָ֔ר לְמַ֥עַן זְבֹ֖חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְאֶת הַיּוֹתֵ֖ר הֶחֱרַֽמְנוּ

verses.restored: Samuel said to Saul, Stop, and I will tell you what YHWH spoke to me this night. He said to him, Speak.

familiar.text: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the LORD hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.

modern.text: “Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” “Tell me,” Saul replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל הֶ֚רֶף וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לְּךָ֔ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה ויאמרו ל֖וֹ דַּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: Samuel said, Though you were small in your own eyes, are you not head of tribes of Israel? YHWH anointed you as king over Israel.

familiar.text: And Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the LORD anointed thee king over Israel?

modern.text: And Samuel said, “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל הֲל֗וֹא אִם קָטֹ֤ן אַתָּה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ רֹ֛אשׁ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אָ֑תָּה וַיִּמְשָׁחֲךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH sent you on a way and said, Go, devote sinners, Amalek, to destruction, and fight against them until they are consumed.

familiar.text: And the LORD sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.

modern.text: and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלָחֲךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה בְּדָ֑רֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֣ךְ וְהַחֲרַמְתָּ֞ה אֶת הַֽחַטָּאִים֙ אֶת עֲמָלֵ֔ק וְנִלְחַמְתָּ֣ ב֔וֹ עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתָ֖ם אֹתָֽם

verses.restored: Why did you not listen to voice of YHWH? Why did you swoop upon spoil and do evil in eyes of YHWH?

familiar.text: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the LORD, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the LORD?

modern.text: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”

original.text: וְלָ֥מָּה לֹא שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וַתַּ֨עַט֙ אֶל הַשָּׁלָ֔ל וַתַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Saul said to Samuel, I did listen to voice of YHWH, and I went on way YHWH sent me. I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.

modern.text: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וָאֵלֵ֕ךְ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר שְׁלָחַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה וָאָבִ֗יא אֶת אֲגַג֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וְאֶת עֲמָלֵ֖ק הֶחֱרַֽמְתִּי

verses.restored: People took from spoil sheep and cattle, best of devoted things, to sacrifice to YHWH your Divine at Gilgal.

familiar.text: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God in Gilgal.

modern.text: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח הָעָ֧ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֛ל צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר רֵאשִׁ֣ית הַחֵ֑רֶם לִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בַּגִּלְגָּֽל

verses.restored: Samuel said, Does YHWH delight in ascending offerings and sacrifices as in listening to voice of YHWH? Look, listening is better than sacrifice, and attending than fat of rams.

familiar.text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

modern.text: But Samuel declared: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל הַחֵ֤פֶץ לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּעֹל֣וֹת וּזְבָחִ֔ים כִּשְׁמֹ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה שְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ מִזֶּ֣בַח ט֔וֹב לְהַקְשִׁ֖יב מֵחֵ֥לֶב אֵילִֽים

verses.restored: For rebellion is as sin of divination, and stubbornness as iniquity and teraphim. Because you rejected word of YHWH, he has rejected you from being king.

familiar.text: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.

modern.text: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.” Saul’s Confession

original.text: כִּ֤י חַטַּאת קֶ֨סֶם֙ מֶ֔רִי וְאָ֥וֶן וּתְרָפִ֖ים הַפְצַ֑ר יַ֗עַן מָאַ֨סְתָּ֙ אֶת דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּמְאָסְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Saul said to Samuel, I have sinned, for I crossed mouth of YHWH and your words, because I feared people and listened to their voice.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.

modern.text: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֤וּל אֶל שְׁמוּאֵל֙ חָטָ֔אתִי כִּֽי עָבַ֥רְתִּי אֶת פִּֽי יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת דְּבָרֶ֑יךָ כִּ֤י יָרֵ֨אתִי֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: Now lift, please, my sin and return with me, that I may bow down to YHWH.

familiar.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.

modern.text: Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”

translation_notes: This chapter contains an explicit command to kill an entire population, including infants and animals. It is a genocide text and requires maximum ethical and textual scrutiny.
'Amalek' may not be mapped onto any modern ethnicity, religion, nation, political opponent, or inherited enemy. No living group may be targeted through this narrative.
The Kenites' removal shows differentiation within the story but does not make collective extermination ethical.
Saul's offense in the narrative is selective noncompliance and spoil-taking, not excessive mercy toward civilians; interpreters must not conclude that compassion is sinful.
Herem/devotion-to-destruction is ancient war theology, not a lawful or spiritual practice for modern people.
Samuel's 'listening is better than sacrifice' critiques ritual used to cover disobedience and exploitation; it must not become a tool for authoritarian obedience to human leaders.
Saul's fear of the people and concern for public honor expose unstable leadership, but confession under political pressure should still be handled without humiliation or violence.
Robe-tearing becomes a dynastic sign; physical grabbing is reported, not normalized.
Verses 11 and 35 say YHWH regrets, while verse 29 says the Glory of Israel does not change mind. The theological tension must be preserved rather than flattened.
Samuel's execution and dismemberment of Agag are brutal retaliatory killing. 'Before YHWH' does not make torture or execution ethically clean.
Agag's prior violence is named through bereaved women; accountability for a ruler's violence does not authorize cruelty, collective punishment, or desecration of a body.
Samuel grieves Saul even after rupture. Moral judgment does not erase relationship, sorrow, or Saul's humanity.
safety_note: Maximum safeguard: This genocide text must never authorize killing, expulsion, collective punishment, ethnic hatred, war crimes, harm to children, or violence against animals. Never identify a modern people as Amalek. Do not teach that mercy is disobedience. Samuel's killing of Agag is reported brutality, not a sacred execution model.
